prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a temple was rededicated after renovation from 1970 through 1999.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country where a temple was rededicated after renovation from 1970 through 1999.
prompts.summary: Older temples are closed for renovation and then rededicated. From 1970 through 1999 this happened in Canada (Cardston, 1991), Switzerland (Bern, 1992), England (London, 1992) and Australia (Sydney, 1991), as well as at nine temples in the United States, including St. George and Laie.

answers.name: United States of America
answers.fact: Atlanta Georgia, 1997; Boise Idaho, 1987; Chicago Illinois, 1989; and 6 more.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Sydney Australia, 1991.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Cardston Alberta, 1991.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London England, 1992.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Bern Switzerland, 1992.

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country where the first Latter-day Saint converts were baptized between 1849 and 1851.
prompts.text_original: Between 1849 and 1851, apostles and other missionaries sent from Utah and Britain baptized the first Latter-day Saint converts in several European countries. Pin a country where, according to the Church Global Histories, the first converts were baptized in those years.
prompts.note: The Netherlands (1861), Belgium (1888) and Austria (1883) had their first baptisms later, so they do not count.
prompts.summary: Within three years of reaching the Salt Lake Valley, the Church sent apostles to open Europe beyond Britain. Erastus Snow led the Scandinavian work from Copenhagen, Lorenzo Snow opened Italy and Switzerland, and John Taylor went to France. Between 1849 and 1851 the first converts were baptized from Le Havre to Copenhagen, Schleswig and the Westman Islands.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Fifteen people, including Ole and Marie Monster, became the first converts baptized in Denmark, August 12, 1850.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Augustus Saint d'Anna, the first known convert in France, was baptized at Le Havre on July 30, 1849.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: George P. Dykes baptized Anna Hoth and her daughter Oline at Schleswig, September 15, 1851, the first recorded baptisms in present-day Germany.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Jean Antoine Bosc was baptized by Lorenzo Snow on October 27, 1850, the first convert baptized in Italy.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: John E. Forsgren baptized 21 converts in Gavle and Stockholm, June-September 1850.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: The first converts in Switzerland were baptized in Geneva in March 1851.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: Hans F. Petersen baptized John Olsen and Peter Adamsen at Risor, November 26, 1851, the first baptisms in Norway.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Benedikt Hansson and Ragnhildur Stefansdottir became the first converts baptized in Iceland, May 1851.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place or people named in the book of Ezra, from Cyrus's Persia to Joppa
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place or people named in the book of Ezra: Cyrus king of Persia, the captives in Babylon, cedar from Lebanon floated to Joppa, the adversaries in Samaria, the roll found at Achmetha in Media, and the peoples Ezra warned against marrying (including Hittites, Ammonites, Moabites and Egyptians)
prompts.note: Samaria is in the West Bank (Palestine); Joppa (Jaffa) is in Israel. Jerusalem is scored as Israel, as in the other Bible prompts.
prompts.summary: Cyrus of Persia let the Jews in Babylon return and rebuild the temple. They paid Zidon and Tyre for cedar from Lebanon, shipped to Joppa, and pressed on despite adversaries who wrote from Samaria to the Persian king. Darius found Cyrus's decree at Achmetha and the temple was finished; later Ezra came to teach the law (Ezra 1-10).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Cyrus king of Persia proclaimed the return, and his decree was found at Achmetha in the province of the Medes (Ezra 1:1-2; 6:2); the Elamites were among Samaria's settlers who wrote against the Jews (Ezra 4:9).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The captives went up from Babylon unto Jerusalem (Ezra 1:11).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: They rebuilt the house of God at Jerusalem, and cedar was brought by sea to Joppa (Ezra 3:7-8).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Meat, drink and oil went to them of Zidon and Tyre for cedar trees from Lebanon (Ezra 3:7).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Egyptians are also in Ezra's list of peoples whose abominations Israel had joined (Ezra 9:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Ezra mourned that the people had mingled with Ammonites and Moabites (Ezra 9:1).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The adversaries wrote to Artaxerxes, and his answer went to Rehum and those dwelling in Samaria (Ezra 4:17).

prompts.display_text: Pin a South Pacific country or territory whose foreign missionaries were called home early in World War II.
prompts.text_original: As World War II spread, the Church called foreign missionaries home from its South Pacific missions in 1940 and early 1941, and local Saints led the branches. Pin a country or territory where a Global Histories chronology records this.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Australia, New Zealand, Tonga, Samoa, French Polynesia)
prompts.note: Hawaii does not count; it received evacuated missionaries. The Samoan Mission covered Samoa and American Samoa, so both count.
prompts.summary: In 1940 the Church withdrew foreign missionaries from its South Pacific missions, and Australia's were gone by January 1941. Local members became branch presidents, mission Relief Society leaders and missionaries. Some evacuated elders were sent on to Hawaii.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Overseas missionaries had been evacuated by January 1941.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: In 1940 leaders told all missionaries in New Zealand to return home.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: 1940: foreign missionaries evacuated; Emile C. Dunn stayed as mission president.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: The Samoa chronology's 1940-45 entry covers the Samoan Islands: missionaries were called home and Samoan Saints led.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: The Tahitian Mission was closed on November 19, 1940; local members led the branches.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: 1940: missionaries of the Samoan Mission called home; Samoan Saints led.

prompts.display_text: Pin an independent South American country in the land Melvin J. Ballard opened to missionaries with a prayer of dedication in 1925
prompts.text_original: On Christmas Day 1925 in Buenos Aires, apostle Melvin J. Ballard dedicated all of South America for the preaching of the gospel. Pin any independent country of South America.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Bolivia, Uruguay, Venezuela)
prompts.note: The prayer covered the whole continent, so every South American country counts. French Guiana is part of France and does not.
prompts.summary: In late 1925 Elder Melvin J. Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles arrived in Buenos Aires to open a South American mission. On December 25 he dedicated the whole continent for the preaching of the gospel. Global Histories chronologies across the continent record that 1925 prayer as the start of Church growth in South America.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Ballard offered the prayer in Buenos Aires in December 1925.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Global Histories (Brazil) lists the 1925 dedication of South America.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Global Histories (Chile) lists the 1925 dedication of South America.

answers.name: Colombia
